It preserves the memories, stories, favorite meals, songs, and traditions of loved ones using Google's open-weight Gemma model, local SQLite storage, and an interactive Digital Ofrenda altar. articles.title: "Context Rot: Test Your App for It, Then Trim What the Model Reads"
articles.excerpt: Your help-desk bot resends the whole conversation every turn. In message three the customer said she is on the annual plan. By message forty she asks for a refund, and the bot quotes the monthly polic…
articles.body: Your help-desk bot resends the whole conversation every turn. In message three the customer said she is on the annual plan. By message forty she asks for a refund, and the bot quotes the monthly policy. The fact was in the prompt the whole time; the model just did not use it. By the end of this post you will have two small scripts that measure whether long context hurts your app, and a short list of moves that trim what the model reads. Here is the video version, with the drawings, if you would rather watch first: What is actually in the context The context is the set of tokens included when you sample from a model: system prompt, chat so far, tool results, documents. And the model keeps no memory of the last turn.

articles.title: How to Export Google Ads Transparency Center Data (with Ad Copy) in Python
articles.excerpt: I wanted something simple: every Google search ad a competitor is running, how long each one has been running, and the actual ad copy — in a spreadsheet. Google already publishes all of this in the Ad…
articles.body: I wanted something simple: every Google search ad a competitor is running, how long each one has been running, and the actual ad copy — in a spreadsheet. Google already publishes all of this in the Ads Transparency Center (Google's answer to Meta's Ad Library). It just has no export button and no API. So I scraped it, and ran into something I didn't expect: for most big advertisers, the ad copy isn't there as text at all . The surprise: most text ads are stored as images When you open a text ad in the Transparency Center, Google renders it in one of two ways: A text preview — the headline and description exist as text (in a small JS preview), easy to parse. A screenshot — a PNG of the ad, nothing else. The words only exist as pixels.

articles.title: Your telemetry doesn't go straight to the backend: Understanding the OpenTelemetry Collector
articles.excerpt: Imagine you run a coffee shop with an online ordering system. A customer orders a cappuccino, completes the payment, and waits for a pickup notification. But the notification never arrives. Your appli…
articles.body: Imagine you run a coffee shop with an online ordering system. A customer orders a cappuccino, completes the payment, and waits for a pickup notification. But the notification never arrives. Your application generates telemetry as it processes the order. Traces capture the request's journey, logs record events, and metrics show how the system behaves. But generating telemetry is only part of the problem. You also need to decide where it goes, what information it contains, and how to deliver it reliably so you can investigate issues. The OpenTelemetry Collector helps you manage these tasks outside your application code. It receives, processes, and exports telemetry, giving you a dedicated layer for controlling your telemetry pipeline.

articles.title: You Built an AI Agent. A Function Would Have Worked.
articles.excerpt: A user asks your app to summarize a document. Your system creates a plan. A planner agent assigns the task to a research agent. A writer agent drafts the summary. A reviewer agent checks the draft. Th…
articles.body: A user asks your app to summarize a document. Your system creates a plan. A planner agent assigns the task to a research agent. A writer agent drafts the summary. A reviewer agent checks the draft. Then another agent decides whether the reviewer is satisfied. Meanwhile, the user is still waiting for five bullet points. Before adding another agent, ask: what decision actually needs one? This is an architectural question worth answering before you build. 1. Separate the uncertain work from the predictable work Consider an invoice-processing feature. Some parts require interpreting messy information: Finding the supplier name in an unfamiliar layout. Understanding a description. Extracting fields from inconsistent documents. Other parts have explicit rules: Is the invoice number present?

articles.body: The ‘70s and ‘80s was a major turning point for science fiction . Star Wars revitalized the genre in 1977 and turned it into one of Hollywood’s main box office draws, inspiring a wave of films that reshaped the entire industry. Two years later, Ridley Scott threw down the gauntlet with Alien , taking a big step away from the optimism that had once permeated sci-fi pulp storytelling and instead infusing it with corporate anxiety and untrustworthy artificial intelligence. It was a signal for things to come.

articles.excerpt: Sir Patrick Stewart is being remembered for Star Trek and X-Men, but he was also the perfect guest star on The Simpsons
articles.body: Yesterday, news broke that Sir Patrick Stewart died at age 86. With his background performing Shakespeare and his incredible sense of dignity and gravitas, Stewart is being celebrated primarily for his work as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation , as well as being the perfect man to portray Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films. But while he was beloved for the dramatic weight he brought to his roles, it's worth acknowledging that the man pulled off some incredibly memorable comedic performances, one of the first was on The Simpsons , where he guest-starred in the season 6 episode, “Homer the Great.”

articles.body: The best twist endings in video games change what you thought you were playing. A great one makes you want to start over to spot the clues, and a perfect one hides those clues in plain sight: in dialogue, in chapter titles, perhaps even the controller you’re holding. These ten games span three decades and nearly every genre, from horror to puzzle-platformers to a Game Boy adventure about a dream. But they all have one thing in common: Every one of them had us totally fooled the first time.

articles.body: If you’re playing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2, beware: you’re at a disadvantage in competitive Multiplayer due to crushing input lag that is much worse than the other platforms. Digital Foundry’s analysis of the performance of the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 — the first Call of Duty released on a Nintendo console since 2013’s Ghosts — found that the input lag on Switch 2 can be two times longer than on PS5 at 60fps. In competitive Multiplayer, Switch 2 aims for 60fps and, according to DF, hits that target most of the time (although some things do cause the frame rate to drop, including looking through the transparent visor of a riot shield).

In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
